title: Out of Boundary Paths
statement:
A grid has `N` rows and `M` columns. A ball sits in the cell at row `Sx`, column `Sy` (both **0-indexed**, row `0` is the top row and column `0` is the leftmost column).

In one move the ball goes to one of the four adjacent cells: up, down, left or right. The ball may move out of the grid, and the move that takes it outside ends its journey; it cannot come back. Moves that stay inside the grid may be repeated freely, including revisiting cells.

Count the number of different sequences of moves that take the ball out of the grid using **at most** `K` moves. Two sequences are different if they differ in the direction of at least one move (or in length). Print the count modulo `10^9 + 7`.
inputFormat: A single line with five integers `N`, `M`, `K`, `Sx` and `Sy`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of move sequences that leave the grid in at most `K` moves, modulo `10^9 + 7`.

examples.explanation: The grid is a single cell, so every one of the 4 directions leaves it in 1 move.

In 1 move: up and left leave the grid (2 sequences). In 2 moves the ball first stays inside by going right to (0,1) or down to (1,0); from either cell two directions leave, giving 4 more sequences. Total 6.
With no moves allowed the ball stays in place.

hints: Let ways[t][i][j] be the number of ways to be at cell (i, j) after exactly t moves while still inside the grid.
A ball on a boundary cell escapes through each missing neighbour. At every step add (ways in that cell × number of directions that leave the grid) to the answer.
You only need the previous layer to compute the next one, so keep two grids. Remember to take everything modulo 10^9 + 7.
